statement: For closed surfaces of every genus at least two, two actual real involutions whose outer actions on the profinite surface group are conjugate have the same real topological type and are discretely conjugate. All six genus-three types therefore remain distinct in the procongruence and full profinite extended mapping class groups.
limitations: Proves injectivity of the known real component classes. Surjectivity onto all profinite involutions and the full centralizer classification remain incomplete.

statement: The injectivity comparison extends to individually labelled real markings and to unordered markings with conjugate pairs. Functorial incidence graphs of all finite compact etale covers identify marked-oval centralizer generators up to exactly the graph sign; the unique diagonal integral homology relation forces simultaneous reversal in the dividing case.
limitations: Does not classify additional profinite involutions. The labelled statement concerns individually real labelled points; unordered nonreal pairs are treated through their quotient-surface interior configurations.

statement: The full-completion to procongruence fibre over a known involution class is the orbit set C_Q(tau_bar) backslash H1(C2,K) under the explicit action q(g).[k]=[g k alpha(g)^-1]. Its centralizer has kernel K^(k tau) and image exactly the stabilizer of [k]. A D8 calculation shows why the orbit and stabilizer cannot be omitted from this general extension computation.
limitations: The mapping-class congruence-kernel orbit sets and fixed subgroups are not evaluated in genus three or higher. The finite example verifies the general formula and is not a counterexample to the requested mapping-class classification.

statement: The completed extended hyperelliptic subgroup embeds in the full genus-three mapping-class completion; all its reflections are discrete up to its own conjugacy, and their centralizers inside this subgroup are closures of the discrete centralizers. Explicit hyperelliptic equations realize all six genus-three real types, so the hyperelliptic intersection of every known real centralizer is computed.
sources: Explicit goodness and real double-cover arguments in C.16
limitations: Computes centralizers only inside the specified closed hyperelliptic subgroup. It does not prove that all ambient reflections belong to such a subgroup or that the whole ambient reflection centralizer lies there.

statement: For each of the five genus-three real types with nonempty real locus, the entire procongruence centralizer is the closure of the discrete centralizer. That closure embeds in the full completion and splits its centralizer map, giving C_hatGamma(tau)=K^tau semidirect closure C_Gamma(tau). The quotient-centralizer action on H1(C2,K) therefore fixes the trivial class.
limitations: The remaining fixed congruence kernel K^tau and the nontrivial H1 orbits are not evaluated. The fixed-point-free genus-three type is excluded. Full profinite surjectivity and the complete ambient centralizer classification remain incomplete.

statement: For the fixed-point-free genus-three involution, the procongruence centralizer is canonically the group of outer automorphisms of the completed quotient-surface group pi1(N4) whose restrictions to the orientation double cover lie in the extended procongruence group. Restriction is first taken modulo the deck involution, then the unique positive representative is selected. The discrete mapping class group of N4 identifies with the ordinary centralizer, so its density is exactly the remaining congruence-centralizer question.
limitations: The statement is an exact comparison, not a density theorem. Density of the nonorientable mapping class group in the displayed automorphism group and the full-completion centralizer remain incomplete.

statement: For every finite-index subgroup H of Mod(N4), the centralizer in the orientation-preserving genus-three mapping class group of its unique positive-lift image has no nonidentity finite-order element. Consequently no such finite-index image centralizes a hyperelliptic involution, and the standard nonorientable hyperelliptic subgroup has infinite index.
sources: Explicit signed pants double and exponent maps in C.19
limitations: Refutes the proposed finite-index hyperelliptic route through an explicit comparison. It does not prove the N4 congruence density equality or classify arbitrary profinite reflections. The graph script certifies only the finite combinatorial part.
